classification.difficultyReason: Derive AE=FC by halving equal opposite sides, retain their parallelism, and apply the standard equal-and-parallel opposite-side test to the indicated quadrilateral.

content.prompt: In the parallelogram $ABCD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $F$ is the midpoint of $CD$. Prove that $AECF$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Parallelogram with midpoint labels E on AB and F on DC, internal segments AF and EC, double parallel arrows on AB/DC and single arrows on AD/BC. Ordinary source blue is rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel and equal to DC; E and F are the specified midpoints.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and segments are visible.

answer.short:
$AE=FC$ and $AE\parallel FC$. Hence $AECF$ is a parallelogram.

One pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel.
answer.worked:
Opposite sides of parallelogram $ABCD$ are equal and parallel, so $AB=CD$ and $AB\parallel CD$.

Since $E$ and $F$ are midpoints,
$$\begin{align*}AE&=\frac12 AB\\FC&=\frac12 CD.\end{align*}$$
Thus $AE=FC$. Also, $AE\parallel FC$, because they lie on $AB$ and $CD$ respectively. Therefore $AECF$ is a parallelogram, since one pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel.
